relevance.rationale: Studies the map from the braid group to the integers sending a braid to the signature of its closure. That map is not a homomorphism, and the article identifies its homomorphism DEFECT with the Meyer cocycle and the Maslov class, and draws consequences for the global geometry of the gordian metric space. The braid-and-closure setting is the corpus's own, and the abstract shape — a closure invariant that fails to be additive under braid concatenation, with the failure measured by a cocycle — is tantalisingly close to the corpus's central many-body question (TjonSimplexForm: 'every nonzero high moment measures non-additivity', mu_3 and mu_4 as deviations from pairwise additivity). But the correspondence is an analogy, not a usable result: the invariant here is the link signature, and grep finds no knot/link signature, no Meyer cocycle and no Maslov class anywhere in content/, computations/ or docs/ — the corpus's closure invariants are the Markov trace and the Jones polynomial. Nothing here transfers without first building a signature layer the corpus does not have. Scope-(a): this document, as read, supplies nothing this folio can consume as-is; it is emphatically NOT a claim that cocycle-valued additivity defects are the wrong frame for the many-body term.

proposedActions.rationale: Read and judged to need nothing today. The honest follow-up, if anyone wants it, is a corpus-side question first — does the Markov-trace binding functional have a 2-cocycle additivity defect at all — and only then a literature match; proposing a citation now would be a wish, not a proposal.
